turns.assessment: The evidence is a hard bidirectional cable break near S20, not a client or optical-card fault. The first span from S20 toward S01 loses OSC (O107), while the corresponding reverse-direction span into S20 loses OSC (O105); downstream amplifier input/preamp LOS occurs simultaneously. The parallel S20–S13 OSC losses are consistent with the same excavation damaging another cable in a shared duct. Stable S20–S04 equipment and pump currents argue against an amplifier or whole-node failure.

proposals.rationale: This is the outbound representation of the physical S20–S01 segment nearest S20. Simultaneous OSC loss here and on the corresponding reverse span oms.S01-S20.span2, together with amplifier LOS in both directions, is the characteristic signature of both fibres of the cable being cut. It explains the loss affecting svc328; the concurrent S20–S13 losses likely reflect collateral damage in the same duct.

This adjacent segment also has bidirectional OSC-loss evidence (O108 and O106), so it was probably cut in the same physical incident. It is less likely to be the principal segment responsible for svc328 than the S20–S01 segment.
